newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HSBC hits record high, more gains seen.
newsitem.headline: HSBC hits record high, more gains seen.

text.p: Shares of HSBC Holdings Plc touched an all-time high of HK$140.50 per share on Monday morning, buoyed by broad market strength and demand from overseas investment funds, brokers said.
The stock stood at HK$140.00 at the midday close, up HK$2.50 or 1.82 percent, and brokers said it had the potential to edge up further after European markets opened later today.

"Solid earnings growth and a relatively low P.E. (price to earnings multiple of about 12), compared with an average P.E. of about 13 times in the overall market, make it an attractive buy," said Ben Kwong, research director at Dharmala Securities.
Kwong said he expected the shares to undergo a correction at around HK$142 to HK$143 before gaining sufficient momentum to edge up again.
Brokers generally said the shares could reach HK$150 in a few weeks and HK$160 within six months where the stock would be fully valued.
